assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishes a general physical-chemical principle for cellular organisation: liquid-liquid phase separation and condensate formation as a way to compartmentalise cells without membranes. It recasts cell biology in terms of phase behaviour, thermodynamics and intermolecular interactions, which is the kind of concept-level reframing of molecular organisation I value most, and it has reshaped research on stress granules, nucleoli and neurodegeneration.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed the P-granule liquid-like behaviour in 2009 and framed the concept; Rosen supplied the multivalent-interaction phase-separation framework for signalling proteins. Pappu and Mittag are strong on the sequence-encoded physics, so the boundary of a trio is a real judgement. Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen is the most defensible three.
assessment.maturity: Concept is now widely adopted and replicated across many systems, but debate persists about which in vivo condensates are truly phase-separated, how material properties matter functionally, and which claims rest on overexpression in vitro. Timely, with the core concept stable even if details are contested.
uncertainties: Unresolved extent to which in vitro droplet behaviour reflects physiological mechanism
Credit split between Hyman/Brangwynne (discovery) and Rosen/Pappu/Mittag (physical framework)
I am relying on my own recollection of the history and have not verified the dates or priorities

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory reduced the protein folding problem to statistical mechanics and thermodynamics, explaining how sequences fold quickly despite astronomical conformational space and giving the field a conceptual basis (frustration, minimal frustration, collapse and hydrophobic effect). This is physical chemistry at its most general and it underpins modern structure prediction and simulation.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are the clearest carriers of the funnel/minimal-frustration framework; Dill contributed the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model foundations. Fersht's experimental mapping (phi-value analysis) is a strong complementary contribution but a different mode, and Bryngelson is credited for early theory. I would keep the theory side.
assessment.maturity: Concept is decades old and broadly confirmed by experiment and simulation; recognition is more than ripe. The 2024 prize for protein structure prediction and design does not fully cover folding physics, so the topic is still open but may feel adjacent.
uncertainties: Possible perception of overlap with 2024 protein-structure prize
Allocation among Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill and Fersht is contested
Dill's inclusion versus Bryngelson/Fersht cannot be settled from the supplied text

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are an applied lipid self-assembly and phase-behaviour achievement: pH-dependent charge, controlled ordering and fusogenicity enable nucleic-acid encapsulation and endosomal release. They enabled siRNA therapeutics and the mRNA vaccines, giving enormous and demonstrated impact, and the physical chemistry is close to my own field of lipid assemblies.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues at UBC developed the core encapsulation and ionizable-lipid concepts and the microfluidic mixing route; Anderson and Langer contributed lipid-library and screening advances. Madden, Hope and MacLachlan are essential collaborators, so credit is spread across many people and companies. A trio of Cullis, Anderson and Hope is a reasonable but contestable option.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale; mature. The 2023 Medicine prize recognised nucleoside modification, not delivery, so delivery chemistry remains unrecognised. Timely.
uncertainties: Credit among UBC, MIT and industrial groups is complex
Distinction between chemistry of ionizable lipids and formulation engineering may weigh on the Chemistry committee
Patent disputes may colour attribution; I cannot verify details

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity through bifunctional degraders and molecular glues created a new pharmacological modality, repurposing the ubiquitin-proteasome system by small-molecule design. It opens a large 'undruggable' target space and has clinical candidates in trials. Conceptually a clear chemical invention with a clean mechanistic basis.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto) made the first PROTACs; Handa/Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target underlying molecular-glue degraders; Ciulli and Gray extended to VHL ligands and other degraders. Three names inevitably leave out important contributors, and the PROTAC versus glue origin may need distinct recognition.
assessment.maturity: Not yet an approved PROTAC drug at the time I recall, so clinical confirmation is still pending, though the biochemical mechanism is strongly established. Possibly slightly early but advancing quickly.
uncertainties: Absence of full clinical validation
Whether a prize should separate PROTACs from thalidomide-type molecular glues
Credit allocation among many contributors is unsettled

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing is a chemical solution to genome editing: engineered deaminases fused to Cas proteins convert bases without double-strand breaks. Its mechanism is clear chemistry, with strong therapeutic reach, and the first clinical results exist. Prime editing (B009) is further, but base editing has more maturity.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory is the clear originator, with Komor and Gaudelli as the lead trainees for cytosine and adenine base editors. A Liu-led prize is possible, though CRISPR was already recognised in 2020, so allocation relative to that prize needs care. Nishida and Kondo had an independent cytidine-deaminase editor, which complicates priority.
assessment.maturity: Clinical translation is under way and the field's replication is excellent; recognition is timely but may be considered premature by some members.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize
Independent Nishida/Kondo work complicates credit
Whether the committee wants to credit trainees

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics unified electronic structure and dynamics, enabling first-principles simulation of liquids, interfaces and reactions, including water and hydrogen bonding that matter for my soft-matter and aqueous-interface interests. Lasting and foundational influence across chemistry, materials and biophysics.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is the decisive contribution and the two-person attribution is unusually clean, which makes a prize configuration straightforward.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with four decades of validation and widespread use; recognition is late rather than premature. The 2013 prize for multiscale models and DFT-related prizes partly cover neighbouring territory.
uncertainties: Possible perceived overlap with earlier computational chemistry prizes
Parrinello also appears on other candidates (metadynamics, ML potentials), which I treat as separate
Recollection of the history is from memory

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite photovoltaics rose from a few percent to above 25 percent efficiency in a decade, creating a major new materials-chemistry platform with defect tolerance and solution processing. The impact on solar energy research is very large and the chemistry is rich.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell in 2009; Park and Snaith made the key solid-state and mesoscopic and thin-film advances that established the efficiency leap; Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel are also major. Allocation is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency and many independent confirmations are robust, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial viability remain unresolved, which argues for caution on timing.
uncertainties: Stability and deployment remain unproven
Credit among Miyasaka, Snaith, Park, Seok and Grätzel is contested
Possible reluctance to reward before technology matures

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami demonstrated programmable self-assembly of arbitrary nanoscale shapes from a long scaffold and short staples, a conceptual and practical advance in controlling molecular organisation. It has spawned a large field from nanorobotics to templating and diagnostics.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 paper is the decisive origin; Seeman's foundational DNA nanotechnology is not in the credited names, and Shih and Yin extended to three dimensions and algorithmic assembly. Winfree and Yan are also important. Credit around the founder is complicated.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated and broadly adopted; applications are still emerging, so recognition may be somewhat early for impact but not for concept.
uncertainties: Foundational contribution by a deceased pioneer who is not in the credited names
Application impact still maturing
Selection of three among five credited names is arguable
